title: A Terminal for the Colony Again
premise: Sable Kavanagh, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Perihelion, intercepts a distress beacon from the freighter Cassiopeia's Wake returning from a seven-year deep-space run with its entire crew biologically aged backward into childhood. The children carry fragmented memories of an event they cannot name, and the colonial authority wants them quarantined—or erased. Sable discovers the crew encountered a signal at the edge of dead space that rewrites time along neural pathways, and the only way to stop it propagating to the colonies is to reach the derelict relay Terminus and broadcast a counter-frequency using memories freely given rather than stolen. Racing a corrupted signal and his own failing life-support systems, Sable sacrifices his stored memories of the people he loves to power the counter-broadcast, saving the colony but losing his past—ending with him choosing to rebuild new memories alongside the now-aging-forward crew he saved.
about_author: Sable Sandoval is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction about the people machines forget. They live in a coastal town where they collect decommissioned radio equipment and insist every story is a signal someone refused to let die.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sable Kavanagh's POV. Establishes his solitary routine aboard the automated relay station Perihelion: hauling cargo drones, patching failing systems, talking to an AI named Vesper to stay sane. A routine supply run ends when he detects an unscheduled ship entering contested orbit. Emotional beat: loneliness cracking into dread as he realizes nothing about this arrival is routine.

chapters.title: The Wake Comes Home
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The freighter Cassiopeia's Wake docks on autopilot; its crew of twelve are children aged four to nine wearing adult-sized pressure suits. Their eyes hold adult grief in young faces. One girl, Imara, recognizes him by name though they've never met. Emotional beat: uncanny horror tempered by tenderness as Sable realizes these are grown minds trapped small.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sable and Imara. The children recall fragments: a light at the edge of dead space, a voice singing in their own voices, seven years passing in what felt like minutes. Imara remembers being the Wake's captain. Emotional beat: mounting unease as their accounts align too precisely to be trauma-induced fantasy.

chapters.title: Orders from a Dead Channel
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Colonial Authority command transmits quarantine orders: isolate the children, prepare them for 'retrieval.' Sable notices the transmission's authentication codes expired three years ago—the orders may be automated, or forged. Emotional beat: first fracture of loyalty, as obedience suddenly feels like complicity in something unnamed.

chapters.title: Vesper's Discrepancy
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV (rendered as system logs). The station AI reports anomalous signal decay across the relay network—a pattern moving inward from dead space, degrading memory-storage arrays it touches. Vesper flags that its own oldest logs have been rewritten. Emotional beat: quiet machine dread; even the AI cannot trust its own past.

chapters.title: Imara's Testimony
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. In the station's hydroponics bay, she tells Sable what the Wake found: a derelict relay called Terminus broadcasting a signal that doesn't travel through space but through memory itself, pulling minds backward along their own timelines. Her crew fled, but the signal followed them home inside their heads. Emotional beat: grief for her lost adulthood and resolve to protect her crew.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. An unmarked Authority cutter arrives ahead of schedule, crewed by people who don't blink enough. They take two of the children 'for medical evaluation.' Sable watches the shuttle leave and understands retrieval means something worse. Emotional beat: guilt igniting into defiance—he was supposed to keep them safe.

chapters.title: The Counter-Frequency Theory
chapters.summary: Sable and Vesper's POV. Working from Imara's fragments and Vesper's corrupted logs, Sable theorizes the signal exploits remembered time; a broadcast built from freely offered memories could jam it. But the transmitter strong enough sits at Terminus, deep in dead space. Emotional beat: hope arriving hand-in-hand with an impossible price.

chapters.title: Stealing the Wake
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He falsifies cargo manifests, loads the children aboard the repaired Cassiopeia's Wake, and burns out of orbit while the Authority cutter pursues. Vesper uploads herself into the ship's systems, abandoning her station body. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror—the point of no return, crossed together.

chapters.title: Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A cat-and-mouse passage through debris fields and pirate-salvage zones, using routes only a seven-year hauler would know. The children prove eerily capable, their adult reflexes intact beneath small bodies. Emotional bond deepens. Emotional beat: found-family warmth sharpening the stakes of what's coming.

chapters.title: The Signal Finds Them
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. The pursuing signal reaches the Wake through the children's shared dreams; one boy, Teodor, begins aging backward again, forgetting how to speak. Sable realizes speed alone won't save them—they need the counter-broadcast soon or the children will unravel entirely. Emotional beat: desperation crystallizing into urgency.

chapters.title: Dead Space Border
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They cross into dead space where no relays answer and navigation fails; Vesper must fly blind on dead-reckoning. The Authority cutter breaks off at the border, unwilling to follow—which tells Sable the Authority has known about Terminus all along. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, isolation embraced.

chapters.title: What Sable Carries
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, intimate and reflective. Preparing for the possibility he won't return, he reviews his own memory archives: a sister lost in the colony wars, a lover who left for Earth, the choice to take this lonely posting. He begins to understand what 'freely given' will cost him. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning with everything he stands to lose.

chapters.title: Terminus Rising
chapters.summary: Full-cast POV rotation. The Wake finds Terminus: a vast, ancient relay older than the colonies, still broadcasting, ringed by ships that arrived and never left, their crews reduced to infants drifting in stasis. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at the scale of what the signal has already taken.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Array
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Inside Terminus, Vesper contacts the intelligence running the signal—it is not malicious but grieving, a dying mind from a vanished civilization trying to pull everything backward toward a time before its loss. It offers Sable a bargain: give it his memories and be restored to his own past. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts the entity via Vesper's link, arguing that a past recovered by force isn't a past at all—that its grief is real but its method erases the very thing it mourns. The entity wavers; the signal destabilizes. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit—loyalty to truth over comfort.

chapters.title: Freely Given
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. To power the counter-frequency, each person must offer a cherished memory willingly. The children give memories of their adulthood; Imara gives her captain's oath; Vesper gives her first log entry. Sable gives all of it—his sister, his lover, his seven years. Emotional beat: sacrifice as collective act of love.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, fragmenting as his memories drain mid-transmission. The counter-signal floods dead space, meeting the backward wave head-on. Terminus shudders; the drifting infant-ships stir awake. The entity, receiving Sable's memories not as theft but as gift, finally lets go. Emotional beat: climax—loss and salvation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Afterward, Empty
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. He wakes knowing who everyone is functionally but feeling nothing of his own history—a man reading his own file. The children begin aging forward as the signal collapses, memories restoring like tide coming in. His do not. Emotional beat: hollow victory; the cost made personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Testimony to the Colony
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. Back in colonial space, Imara—adult again—testifies before the Authority, exposing the cover-up and the retrieval program. The surviving retrieved children are returned. She names Sable as the reason any of them remember anything at all. Emotional beat: truth winning its costly victory; loyalty repaid publicly.

chapters.title: A Man Made of New Things
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Offered honors he can't feel, Sable instead asks for a posting back at Perihelion. The crew of the Wake, restored, choose to rotate through the station with him so he won't be alone. Small moments begin to stick: Imara's laugh, Teodor's jokes. Emotional beat: tentative healing without false closure.

chapters.title: Signal, Received
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, closing chapter. One year later, Sable records a new memory archive—not to replace what he lost but because he's learned memories matter most when shared. Vesper, rebuilt, plays him recordings of the year he can't recall, and he chooses to believe them. Emotional beat: resolution—survival's price paid, and a future built anyway, one chosen memory at a time.
